Observations:  
- Channel 0 (agent) has large weights across the playable 8Ã8 area, but there are clear âholesâ where the weights are near zero. These holes form a fixed internal wall pattern: e.g. (2,2)=0.41, (2,3)=0.41, (2,6)=0.35, (2,7)=0.35, (3,2)=0.36, (3,7)=0.31, (4,4)=0.29, (4,5)=0.37, (5,4)=0.42, (5,5)=0.36, (6,2)=0.43, (6,7)=0.32, (7,2)=0.32, (7,3)=0.34, (7,6)=0.33, (7,7)=0.32. The agent is never in those cells, so they are walls.  
- Channel 1 (moving objects) has strong weights in many non-wall cells, e.g. (4,7)=8.93, (5,7)=8.21, (7,5)=8.13, (3,3)=7.77. These are movable objects other than the agent.  
- Channel 2 (reward targets) is sparse and has two very large peaks: (2,4)=4.90 and (6,4)=4.50. These look like fixed target squares.  
- Channel 3 (obstacles) has uniformly small weights, max 0.49. The walls are constant, so the network largely ignores this channel and instead learns the fixed wall layout implicitly through the agent-position holes.  
- Channel 4 (previous frame) tracks previous agent/moving-object positions, consistent with needing to remember what just moved.  
- Output biases: b3 = [-0.873, 0.703, 0.712, 0.595, -0.092]. No-op is discouraged, while up/down/left are favored; right is slightly negative. This fits a game where the agent must actively navigate a grid.

Reasoning:  
The combination of a fixed internal wall maze, a channel for movable non-agent objects, and a very sparse reward-target channel with two fixed target cells is characteristic of Sokoban. In Sokoban, the agent pushes boxes onto target squares; walls block movement; boxes are the âmoving objectsâ that move only when pushed. Games like Pac-Man would have many reward pellets, Fetch would have one movable object and one goal, and Dynamic-Obstacles would have moving hazards rather than pushable boxes. The wall pattern and two targets strongly match a Sokoban-style puzzle.

Game: Sokoban.

Description: The agent moves around a fixed maze and pushes boxes onto target squares. Reward is given when boxes are placed on the target cells.

Confidence: 95%
